node.label: GNPTG-mucolipidosis
node.definition: A very rare lysosomal disease, that has most often been observed in the Middle East, characterized by a progressive slowing of the growth rate in early childhood; stiffness and pain in shoulders, hips, and finger joints; a gradual, mild coarsening of facial features; and by a slower progression, milder clinical course and longer life expectancy than that seen in mucolipidosis II and mucolipidosis III alpha/beta. Cognitive function is normal or only slightly impaired and retinitis pigmentosa has been reported in a few patients. Many survive into early adulthood, but ultimately succumb to cardiorespiratory insufficiency.

mechanism_classes.label: lysosomal storage (degradation inside the lysosome fails)

evidence.snippet: Disease-causing germline mutation(s) (loss of function) in (Assessed) — N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate transferase subunit gamma
